$comment: Single source of truth for every error hookrisk can emit.
The Python detectors (detectors/slither_hookrisk/utils/diagnostics.py) and the
TypeScript CLI (cli/src/errors.ts) both load this file, so a message can never
drift between the two runtimes. docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md is generated from it by
scripts/gen_error_docs.py, and CI fails if the generated file is stale.
Fields:
code      Stable identifier. Never reuse or renumber; retire instead.
title     One line, imperative or declarative, no trailing period.
cause     Why this happens, in terms of what the user did or their environment.
fix       Ordered, concrete remediation steps. First entry is the usual fix.
match     Regexes tested against raw tool output to auto-classify a failure.
exitCode  Process exit status. Distinct ranges make CI assertions readable.
seeAlso   Optional links to upstream issues or docs.
Ranges: 0xx environment, 1xx configuration, 2xx compilation/static analysis,
3xx harness execution, 4xx network and explorers, 5xx manifest and scoring,
9xx internal.
Exit codes intentionally avoid 1: a bare 1 is what an uncaught crash produces,
so reserving it lets CI distinguish 'hookrisk reported a problem' from
'hookrisk itself broke'. Exit code 2 is reserved for 'scan completed and the
risk gate failed', which is a successful run, not an error. Exit code 64 is
sysexits.h EX_USAGE: the command line itself was wrong, so no scan was even
attempted. It has no HR-E entry because there is nothing to diagnose — the
usage text is the whole message.

reserved.2: scan completed, risk gate failed — this is a result, not an error
reserved.64: usage: unknown command, or no command at all (sysexits.h EX_USAGE)

errors.title: Foundry is not installed or not on PATH
errors.cause: hookrisk shells out to `forge` to compile the target and to run the differential harness. Neither the static nor the dynamic layer can start without it.
fix: Install Foundry: `curl -L https://foundry.paradigm.xyz | bash && foundryup`
Reopen your shell, or `source ~/.bashrc` / `source ~/.zshenv`, so PATH picks it up.
Verify with `forge --version`. hookrisk requires 1.0.0 or newer.
In CI, use `foundry-rs/foundry-toolchain@v1` before calling hookrisk.

errors.title: Slither is not installed or not importable
errors.cause: The static layer is a Slither detector plugin. Without Slither, hookrisk can still run the harness and score declared dimensions, but every measured static dimension would be unscored — so it stops rather than emit a manifest that silently understates risk.
fix: `pipx install slither-analyzer` (recommended — keeps it off your system Python).
Or, inside a virtualenv: `pip install slither-analyzer`.
Then install the plugin: `pip install ./detectors` from the repo root.
Verify with `slither --list-detectors | grep hookrisk`.
To deliberately score without static analysis, pass `--skip-static`. The manifest records `staticAnalysis.skipped: true` and the affected dimensions are reported as unmeasured, never as zero.

errors.title: Python version is unsupported
errors.cause: The detector plugin uses `match` statements and PEP 604 unions, and Slither itself requires a modern runtime.
fix: Install Python 3.10 or newer.
Confirm the interpreter Slither actually uses: `slither --version` then `python3 -c 'import sys; print(sys.version)'`.
A pipx install pins its own interpreter, which is usually the cleanest fix on macOS where the system Python is old.

errors.title: The hookrisk Slither plugin is installed but not registered
errors.cause: Slither discovers plugins through the `slither_analyzer.plugin` entry point. If the package was installed into a different environment than the one running Slither, the detectors are on disk but invisible.
fix: Check they are registered: `slither --list-detectors | grep HS-`.
If nothing prints, install into the same environment: `python -m pip install ./detectors` using the interpreter that owns Slither.
With pipx, inject rather than install: `pipx inject slither-analyzer ./detectors`.
Editable installs (`pip install -e ./detectors`) do register entry points, but only after the environment is restarted.

errors.title: hookrisk cannot find its own installation
errors.cause: The CLI is one part of hookrisk. The differential harness is a Foundry project under `harness/` and the manifest schema and framework rubric are JSON under `schema/`, and the CLI reads all three at runtime. It finds them by walking up from its own `dist/` directory, which only works when it is run from a checkout that `make setup` has prepared. A copied `dist/`, a global `npm install` of the package alone, or a partial checkout leaves it with nothing to run.
fix: From a hookrisk checkout, run `make setup`. It creates the virtualenv, materialises the pinned Solidity dependencies into `harness/lib/`, registers the detectors and builds the CLI.
If the CLI lives somewhere else on purpose, point it at the checkout: `export HOOKRISK_HOME=/path/to/hookrisk`.
Confirm the directory really is one: it must contain both `harness/foundry.toml` and `schema/`.
hookrisk is not published to npm today; see docs/ARCHITECTURE.md for what a split into a standalone package would require.

errors.title: hookrisk.toml is missing a required declared dimension
errors.cause: The Uniswap Foundation framework scores nine dimensions. Some are measurable from code; the rest — team maturity above all — are self-declared by definition. hookrisk refuses to invent them, because a fabricated declaration produces a total score that looks authoritative and is not.
fix: Run `hookrisk init` to generate a commented hookrisk.toml with every declared field and the framework's own scoring brackets inline.
Fill in `[declared] teamMaturity` (0-3) and `[declared] tvlPotential` (0-5) at minimum.
See docs/SCORING.md for which dimensions hookrisk measures and which it cannot.
There is deliberately no default. See FEEDBACK.md #3 for why defaulting these would undermine the framework.

errors.title: Target hook could not be resolved
errors.cause: The scan target must be either `path/to/File.sol:ContractName` for source mode, or a `0x`-prefixed 20-byte address plus `--chain` for deployed mode. Anything else is ambiguous.
fix: Source mode: `hookrisk scan src/MyHook.sol:MyHook`.
Deployed mode: `hookrisk scan 0xabc...123 --chain base`.
If the contract name is omitted and the file declares exactly one contract, hookrisk uses it; if the file declares several, name the one you mean.
Run `hookrisk targets src/MyHook.sol` to list the contracts hookrisk can see in a file.

errors.title: Declared fee bound is missing while the hook can alter fees
errors.cause: Invariant I2 asserts that a swap through the hooked pool returns at least what the vanilla pool returns, less the fee the hook declares it charges. Without a declared bound there is no threshold to test against, and any extraction at all would look legitimate.
fix: Set `[declared] maxFeeBps` in hookrisk.toml to the largest fee your hook can ever charge, in basis points.
If the hook charges no fee of its own, set it to 0 explicitly — that is a much stronger assertion and hookrisk will hold you to it.
If the hook implements a custom curve (a returns-delta permission), I2 does not apply; hookrisk substitutes price monotonicity plus I1 and I3. See docs/INVARIANTS.md.

errors.title: Foundry library path is parent-relative and Slither cannot resolve it
errors.cause: crytic-compile, which Slither uses to drive Foundry, does not normalise `..` segments in `libs`. Compilation succeeds, then name resolution fails on an inherited interface, and the abort message names an arbitrary contract rather than the real problem. Observed with `libs = ["../harness/lib"]` compiling v4-core, which aborts with `AssertionError: Contract IExttload not found`.
fix: Replace the parent-relative entry with a symlink inside the project: `ln -s ../shared/lib lib`, then `libs = ["lib"]`.
Or vendor the dependencies into the project directly.
This is an upstream limitation, not a problem with your contracts — the same tree compiles fine under `forge build`.
hookrisk's own corpus uses the symlink approach; see corpus/foundry.toml.
match: Failed to resolved name for reference id

errors.title: Foundry test path shadows the source path, so nothing is analysed
errors.cause: crytic-compile builds with `forge build --build-info --skip ./<test>/** --skip ./<script>/** --force`. When `test` in foundry.toml points at the same directory as `src`, every contract is skipped and `--force` clears any earlier artifacts. Slither then finds no build-info and reports either a hard failure or, worse, a clean scan of nothing.
fix: Give `test` its own directory in foundry.toml, even if it is empty.
Confirm the build actually produced artifacts: `ls out/build-info` should contain a JSON file after `forge build --build-info`.
If your project genuinely keeps tests beside sources, pass `--foundry-compile-all` so crytic-compile omits the skip flags.

errors.title: Target compiles under forge but not under Slither
errors.cause: Slither parses solc's AST, which is stricter about some constructs than code generation is, and it does not support every solc version the moment that version ships.
fix: Confirm the baseline: `forge build --build-info --force` on its own.
Pin a solc version Slither supports in foundry.toml, e.g. `solc = "0.8.26"`.
Try `--ignore-compile` after a manual `forge build --build-info` so Slither reuses your artifacts instead of rebuilding.
If it still fails, `--skip-static` produces a manifest from the harness alone, with every static dimension marked unmeasured.
match: Compilation failed\. Can you run build command\?

errors.title: Static analysis could not lift every function to IR
errors.cause: Slither failed to build SlithIR for one or more functions and continued anyway, logging `Impossible to generate IR for <function>`. Those functions were never analysed. Reporting the scan as clean would be a false negative dressed up as a pass — observed on OpenZeppelin's own AntiSandwichHook, where three functions including `_afterSwap` fail to lift.
fix: Read the affected function manually. hookrisk lists every skipped function in the manifest under `staticAnalysis.uncoveredFunctions` and in HOOK_RISK.md.
Try a different solc version in foundry.toml; IR lifting failures are often version specific.
The dynamic layer is unaffected — the differential harness executes the real bytecode, so invariants I1-I3 still cover these paths.
Pass `--fail-on-partial-coverage` to make this a hard failure instead of a warning. Appropriate for a release gate on your own hook; too strict for scanning third-party code.
Please report the function upstream at https://github.com/crytic/slither/issues — these are upstream bugs and they are fixable.

errors.title: Hook source not found for a deployed address
errors.cause: Deployed-mode scanning fetches verified source from the block explorer. Unverified contracts have none, so hookrisk falls back to bytecode-only analysis with reduced confidence.
fix: This is a warning by default, not a failure — the manifest records `sourceAvailable: false` and lowers the confidence of every affected finding.
Set `ETHERSCAN_API_KEY` for the multichain V2 endpoint; without a key you are heavily rate limited.
hookrisk falls back to Sourcify automatically when the explorer has nothing.
Pass `--require-source` to make this a hard error instead, which is the right setting for a CI gate on your own contracts.

errors.title: Differential harness could not deploy the hook at a flag-bearing address
errors.cause: v4 reads a hook's permissions from the low 14 bits of its address. The harness uses `deployCodeTo` to place the hook at an address carrying exactly the flags it declares, which requires the compiled artifact to be on disk under the name the harness expects.
fix: Build first: `forge build` in the project containing the hook.
Check that `getHookPermissions()` returns the permissions the hook actually implements — a mismatch here is HS-02, and it makes the address unconstructible.
If the hook's constructor calls `Hooks.validateHookPermissions`, it will revert at a mismatched address; that revert is the intended behaviour and the finding is real.
See docs/INVARIANTS.md for how the twin pools are constructed.

errors.title: Invariant run found a counterexample
errors.cause: This is a result, not a malfunction. One of I1 (conservation), I2 (undeclared extraction) or I3 (exit liveness) failed, and the manifest carries the shrunk call sequence that reproduces it.
fix: Read the counterexample: `hook-risk.json` → `invariants[].counterexample` holds the calldata sequence.
Reproduce it in isolation: `forge test --match-test <name> -vvvv` inside harness/.
I3 failures mean a liquidity provider could not withdraw. Treat as critical until proven otherwise.
I2 failures may be a missing or understated `maxFeeBps` declaration rather than a bug — check the declaration first, and if the fee is real and intended, declare it.

errors.title: Harness timed out before completing its sequences
errors.cause: The `scan` profile is bounded for CI. A hook with expensive callbacks, or a very deep external-call graph, can exceed the budget.
fix: Raise the budget: `--timeout 900` (seconds).
Reduce sequence depth for a first pass: `FOUNDRY_PROFILE=scan forge test --invariant-depth 16`.
Partial results are still written; the manifest marks the affected invariants `inconclusive`, which is deliberately not the same as `passed`.
For a pre-deployment run use `FOUNDRY_PROFILE=deep` locally rather than widening the CI budget.

errors.title: Differential harness could not set up the twin pools
errors.cause: The hook was deployed, but building the pools around it failed: pool initialisation or the initial PoolManager liquidity reverted inside a hook callback, or forge exited before running a single sequence. Nothing about the hook's behaviour was observed. hookrisk reports this as a harness failure with every invariant `inconclusive` — deliberately not `passed`, and deliberately not absent, because a dynamic layer that did not run must not look like one that ran and found nothing. This is an engine result recorded in the manifest (engines[].errorCode), not a CLI abort: the process exit code is decided by the gate, which fails on it by default (failOnNotAnalysed) and exits 2.
fix: Read the unwrapped revert in the reason: it names the callback (e.g. `beforeAddLiquidity (0x259982e5)`) and the hook's own error, decoded from v4's ERC-7751 `WrappedError` wrapper.

A hook that rejects PoolManager liquidity by design (a custom-curve hook holding its own reserves) is handled: the harness records `seeded = "hooked-failed"` and hookrisk marks I2/I3 not-applicable rather than failing. If you see this error instead, the harness in use predates that record — rebuild from the same checkout as the CLI.
A hook that reverts on a static LP fee is retried with `LPFeeLibrary.DYNAMIC_FEE_FLAG`; a revert on both means the hook's `beforeInitialize` needs state the harness does not provide.
Reproduce in isolation: `HOOKRISK_ARTIFACT=... forge test --match-contract GenericHookInvariants -vvvv` inside harness/, with the same environment the CLI logs under `--verbose`.

errors.title: Hook constructor arguments could not be derived
errors.cause: The harness deploys the hook itself, so it has to supply whatever the constructor takes. It can derive two shapes on its own — no arguments, or a single `IPoolManager`/`address` — and needs to be told about anything else. This is reported as a skip with the ABI types in the message rather than guessed, because a constructor fed zero addresses produces a hook that reverts somewhere inside `setUp` for a reason nobody can read. This is an engine result recorded in the manifest (engines[].errorCode), not a CLI abort: the process exit code is decided by the gate, which fails on it by default (failOnNotAnalysed) and exits 2.
fix: Add `[harness] constructorArgs` to hookrisk.toml: an array of strings, one per constructor argument in ABI order.

Use the placeholders for anything the harness deploys itself: `$poolManager`, `$currency0`, `$currency1`, `$owner` (the test contract) and `$hook` (the hook's own flag-bearing address). Each is substituted word-for-word before deployment.

Write every other value the way `cast abi-encode` accepts it — decimal integers, 0x-prefixed addresses and bytes, `true`/`false`. The values are passed to cast verbatim; a cast parse error is repeated in the skip reason.
Struct (tuple) constructor arguments are not supported yet; the skip reason says so when that is the case.

errors.title: RPC endpoint is unset or unreachable
errors.cause: Deployed-mode and fork-mode scanning need an archive-capable RPC for the target chain.
fix: Set the endpoint: `export BASE_RPC_URL=https://...` (or `UNICHAIN_RPC_URL`, `MAINNET_RPC_URL`).
Public endpoints frequently refuse wide `eth_getLogs` ranges; the crawler chunks automatically, but a dedicated endpoint is far faster.
Verify independently: `cast block-number --rpc-url $BASE_RPC_URL`.
Source-mode scanning needs no RPC at all — omit `--chain` to stay offline.

errors.title: Explorer API rejected the request
errors.cause: Source fetching uses the Etherscan V2 multichain API, which takes one key across chains via the `chainid` parameter. A missing key still works but at a rate limit low enough to fail on any real crawl.
fix: Set `ETHERSCAN_API_KEY`. One key covers every supported chain on V2.
On HTTP 429, hookrisk retries with exponential backoff; a persistent 429 means the key is exhausted.
Sourcify is tried automatically when the explorer returns nothing, and needs no key.
Use `--cache-dir` to reuse fetched sources across runs instead of re-fetching.

errors.title: Codehash changed between scan and report
errors.cause: A manifest is bound to one `(chainId, address, codehash)` triple. If the code at the address changed mid-scan the manifest would describe contracts that no longer exist — which is precisely the upgrade scenario the binding exists to catch.
fix: Re-run the scan against the new code.
If the hook is upgradeable, this is expected on every upgrade and is exactly why HS-04 raises the tier: a manifest cannot outlive the code it describes.
Publish an upgrade policy and re-scan as part of it — the framework's Upgradeable trigger requires this anyway.
For reproducible reporting, pin a block: `--block <number>`.

errors.title: Generated manifest does not validate against the schema
errors.cause: An internal inconsistency: hookrisk produced a manifest its own schema rejects. Downstream consumers rely on the schema, so emitting it anyway would push the failure onto them.
fix: This is a bug in hookrisk. Please open an issue with the full output.
Attach the rejected manifest: it is written to `hook-risk.invalid.json` for exactly this purpose.
As a workaround, `--no-validate` emits it regardless. Do not feed the result to a gate.

errors.title: Risk gate threshold not met
errors.cause: Not an error. The scan completed and the resulting tier or findings exceeded the configured gate, so the CI step fails on purpose.
fix: Read HOOK_RISK.md for the tier and the findings that drove it.
Fix the findings, or raise the threshold deliberately in hookrisk.toml `[gate] maxTier`.
To report without gating, pass `--no-gate`; the manifest is still produced.
A rising tier after a code change is the tool working. Re-scoring downward without changing the code is the failure mode the framework warns about.

errors.title: Unexpected internal error
errors.cause: hookrisk hit a state it does not have a specific diagnosis for.
fix: Re-run with `--verbose` to get the full stack trace and the exact tool invocations.
Please open an issue with that output; an unmapped failure is a gap in this catalogue and we treat it as a bug.
`--debug-dir <path>` dumps every intermediate artifact (build-info, Slither JSON, forge output) for attaching to the report.
